legalBasis: NIRC Sec 24(A)(2)(a), as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN); rates effective Jan 1, 2023 onward
graduatedBrackets.notes: Base is the tax on the bracket floor; rate applies to the excess over the floor. Watch: the post-SONA 2026 package would change this table from TY2027 if enacted: HB 10345 (₱350k zero bracket) cleared the House Ways & Means committee Aug 10, 2026; Senate counterparts SB 2338 (₱350k) and SB 1685 (₱500k) pending. Not enacted as of the October 7, 2026 review (latest report Oct 1, 2026); re-verify before the 2027 tax year.

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 24(A)(2)(b), as amended by RA 10963
eightPercent.notes: In lieu of both graduated income tax and the Sec 116 percentage tax. Unavailable to VAT-registered taxpayers, those over the ₱3M threshold, those subject to other percentage taxes (Secs 117-127), GPP partners, and income-tax-exempt individuals such as registered BMBEs (RMO 23-2018). Mixed-income earners get no extra ₱250,000 reduction on the business side; it is embedded in the graduated computation of their compensation income. Elected each year on or before the first quarterly filing (1701Q, or 2551Q if earlier) or via Form 1905; irrevocable for the year. Breaching ₱3M mid-year puts the ENTIRE year back on graduated rates (8% payments become credits) plus percentage tax until VAT registration.

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 34(L), as amended by RA 9504
osd.notes: For individuals, OSD is 40% of gross sales/receipts (corporations compute it on gross income instead). Election is irrevocable for the taxable year.

legalBasis: RR 16-2008 (not claimable while on OSD; the 3 years still run)
netOperatingLossCarryOver.notes: A net operating loss of the business (itemized deductions above gross income) is carried over as a deduction from business income for the next 3 years, only in years the taxpayer itemizes; it cannot be used while on the OSD or the 8% option, and those years still count toward the 3. The estimator applies prior-year NOLCO to the itemized option only and never against compensation income (owner decision 16; whether a mixed-income earner's business loss may reduce compensation was not confirmed from a primary source, REVIEW.md 4.2). The 5-year period for 2020 and 2021 losses (RA 11494) is shown as 'check with your CPA'.

value.method: 49 centavos or less drop, 50 or more round up, per form line

legalBasis: BIR Forms 1700, 1701, 1701A and 1701Q (January 2018): "DO NOT enter Centavos; 49 Centavos or Less drop down; 50 or more round up"
returnLineRounding.notes: Every amount on an income tax return is a whole peso. The estimators round each line (gross, deduction, taxable income, tax due, percentage tax, credits) and add the rounded lines for totals, so the figures match what goes on the form (re-checked Oct 7, 2026; REVIEW.md rules table 2.1).

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 32(B)(7)(e), as amended by RA 10963
thirteenthMonthExclusionCap.notes: 13th month pay and other benefits excluded from gross income up to ₱90,000 per year, unchanged through 2026 (excess de minimis counts toward this cap). Watch: a House committee proposal would raise it to ₱120,000 alongside the TY2027 bracket package; not enacted as of the October 7, 2026 review.

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 56(A)(2), as amended by RA 10963
annualITRInstallment.notes: When annual income tax due exceeds ₱2,000, individuals may pay in two equal installments: at filing, and on or before October 15.

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 232, as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN)
RR 8-2018 (8% filers keep books but need no audited FS)
NIRC Sec 34(L) (OSD filers need not submit FS)
afsRequiredAboveGross.notes: Books audited by an independent CPA required when gross annual sales exceed ₱3,000,000, a threshold TRAIN set in 2018, replacing the old ₱150,000-per-quarter trigger; the ₱3M audit line has stood unchanged since, though EOPT layered simplified bookkeeping rules for micro and small taxpayers on top. Individuals validly on the 8% option or claiming the OSD are not required to submit audited FS; confirm applicability with your CPA.
